channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes diz que errou ao citar homossexualidade em críticas a Zema
item.description: Justice Gilmar Mendes admitted he erred by linking homosexuality to an accusation against Romeu Zema in a Metrópoles interview, later apologizing. The incident occurred amid Mendes’ request to include Zema in the fake news investigation, based on a video where Zema criticizes the STF, portraying justices as puppets. Zema said he was not notified and criticized the STF’s lack of due process in secretive investigations.

item.title: TSE publica acórdão de julgamento que condenou Castro e reconhece renúncia do ex-governador
item.description: The TSE published the ruling that convicted former governor Cláudio Castro of abuse of political and economic power in the 2022 elections, declaring him ineligible for eight years, but recognized that the vacancy of the office was due to resignation, not cassation of the diploma. This leaves open the method for selecting the interim governor in Rio de Janeiro, currently under the responsibility of the TJ-RJ president, as the final decision rests with the STF, where Minister Flávio Dino is still reviewing the case.

item.title: Presidente da Alerj pede ao STF para assumir governo interino do Rio
item.description: The president of the Rio de Janeiro State Legislative Assembly (Alerj), Douglas Ruas (PL), asked the STF to authorize him to act as interim governor until the Court rules on the elections for a caretaker mandate of the state executive.

item.title: Lula: temos que fazer as pessoas lerem mesmo se não tiverem condições de comprar livros
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that the government aims to ensure access to books even for those who cannot afford to buy them, speaking alongside Chamber President Hugo Motta. He described this goal as a shared challenge between the Executive and Legislative branches.

item.title: Lulômetro: Desaprovação do Governo chega a 50% pela primeira desde julho de 2025
item.description: Disapproval of President Lula's government reached 50% for the first time since July 2025, according to the Lulômetro by O Antagonista and Real Time Big Data. 27% of respondents rated the administration as excellent or good, 22% as fair, and 1% did not answer. This marks the lowest approval level since the start of his third term.

item.title: Lula realizará procedimentos médicos em São Paulo nesta sexta-feira
item.description: President Lula will undergo medical procedures at São Paulo's Hospital Sírio-Libanês on Friday, including removal of a scalp keratosis and a right wrist injection for tendinitis treatment. He arrived in São Paulo on Thursday night and is expected to stay through the weekend, with uncertain participation in the PT Congress closing in Brasília on Sunday.

item.title: “Sou muito seguro da minha sexualidade”, diz Zema
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) responded to Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes, who had compared a satirical animation made by Zema about the Court to a potential depiction of the politician as homosexual. Zema stated he is 'very sure of my sexuality' and criticized the comparison as inappropriate, emphasizing that it is incorrect to equate homosexuality with something negative or derogatory.

item.title: Gilmar caçoa e afirma que Zema fala “em dialeto”
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes mocked former governor Romeu Zema, saying he often does not understand Zema's way of speaking, comparing it to a dialect similar to Portuguese. The comment was made in Wednesday interviews, after Mendes had requested Zema be included in the Fake News investigation.

item.title: Douglas Ruas vai ao STF e se reúne com Zanin em articulação para assumir governo do Rio
item.description: Douglas Ruas, president of the Rio de Janeiro Legislative Assembly, met with Supreme Court Minister Cristiano Zanin to seek assumption of the state government, arguing that the vacancy in the Assembly presidency that justified the TJ-RJ president's interim governorship no longer exists. The move follows the Assembly's petition to the STF for immediate inauguration, while Zanin reportedly awaits action from Minister Dino and the TSE's ruling on whether the election will be direct or indirect.

item.title: Motta diz a ministros que vai dar celeridade a projeto que reduz imposto sobre combustíveis
item.description: House Speaker Hugo Motta pledged to expedite a bill reducing federal taxes on fuels, especially gasoline, to counter the impact of the Middle East war on prices and President Lula’s popularity in an election year. The bill, already filed, is expected to be fast-tracked for direct floor vote under urgency procedures, with rapporteur and voting schedule to be set after the upcoming leaders’ meeting on Tuesday.

item.title: PT vai ao TSE e pede suspensão de perfil fake nas redes que fazia ataques a Lula
item.description: The PT, PV, and PCdoB filed a representation with the TSE requesting the suspension of AI-generated social media profiles named 'Dona Maria' that attacked President Lula and other left-wing politicians without disclosing their artificial nature. The parties claim the profiles were designed to appear as real individuals and were used to spread falsehoods, decontextualized information, and commit honor crimes, constituting illegal political propaganda under anonymity.

item.title: Douglas Ruas se reúne com Zanin em meio à indefinição sobre sucessão no Rio
item.description: Douglas Ruas, president of the Alerj, met with Minister Cristiano Zanin (STF) to seek clarification on his potential assumption as interim governor of Rio de Janeiro, following the suspension of the indirect election for the temporary mandate. Zanin reiterated he will not change his position until the judgment is resumed, awaiting the TSE’s publication of the acórdão on Castro’s ineligibility. The conflict arises from a divergence between the Federal Constitution (which mandates indirect elections in the last two years of term) and the Electoral Code (which requires direct elections when more than six months remain in the term).

item.title: Diante de Romeu Zema, Flávio Bolsonaro vai ser obrigado a se mexer e a falar do STF
item.description: Minas Gerais Governor Romeu Zema has emerged as a leading critic of the STF, setting the agenda for Brazil's right-wing discourse and forcing Flávio Bolsonaro to respond. Andreazza argues Zema aims to be seen as courageous in challenging the Supreme Court, while Bolsonaro is viewed as passive and lacking conviction. This pressure compels Bolsonaro to break his silence and address the STF, despite his preference to appear moderate.

item.title: Lula diz que cabe aos homens combater a violência contra mulheres
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) called on men to combat violence against women during the Vivaleitura Prize ceremony, stating that the fight against gender-based violence is men’s responsibility, as they are the perpetrators. He referenced the Brazil Pact to Combat Femicide and said he will read the biography of Gisèle Pelicot, a global symbol in the fight against sexual violence. The event also featured the signing of the new National Book and Reading Plan (PNLL) 2026-2035, aiming to increase the share of the population with a reading habit from 47% to 55% by 2035.

item.title: Valdemar entra em cena por Douglas Ruas no governo do RJ
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the PL party, met with STF Minister Cristiano Zanin to request that Douglas Ruas, newly elected president of the Rio de Janeiro Legislative Assembly, assume the state government on an interim basis. The request is tied to a legal action challenging the validity of an indirect election for the governorship.

item.title: PT faz 8º Congresso dividido sobre aliança com a direita e ruptura com atual modelo econômico
item.description: The PT held its 8th Congress in Brasília, divided between forming strategic alliances with the right to counter bolsonarism and breaking with the current economic model. The most contentious discussions were postponed until after the October elections, with Lula’s faction claiming a majority to approve the alliances. The party avoids mentioning the INSS scandal in its initial platform, instead attributing 'institutional capture' to the Bolsonaro government and highlighting the Banco Master case as justification for financial reform.

item.title: Zema confunde Planalto com Alvorada em vídeo de campanha
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo-MG pre-candidate for Presidency, mistakenly referred to the Palácio do Planalto as the Palácio da Alvorada in a campaign video, confusing the federal government’s seat with the president’s official residence. The video promotes his 'Brazil Without Untouchables' platform, targeting perceived privileges in the Executive, Legislature, and STF, while emphasizing his austere lifestyle — traveling by car and avoiding corporate cards for personal expenses. The gaffe comes amid rising tensions with STF Minister Gilmar Mendes, who responded to Zema’s 'corrupt' remarks about the Court by pushing for his inclusion in the fake news investigation led by Alexandre de Moraes.

item.title: “Times Square” de Nunes fechará vias para carros em SP
item.description: The 'Times Square' São Paulo project will partially close São João and Ipiranga avenues to cars on weekends starting late August 2026, featuring cultural attractions, small music stages, and up to 2,000 m² of LED panels on buildings in the area. Announced by Mayor Ricardo Nunes and Governor Tarcísio de Freitas, the initiative partners with Fábrica de Bares, which will restore the region and install four panels in exchange for a R$6 million private investment, with 70% of panel content dedicated to digital arts and cultural events, and restrictions on retail pricing ads, gambling, and adult content.

item.title: Nunes e Tarcísio anunciam ‘Times Square’ no centro de SP
item.description: São Paulo Mayor Ricardo Nunes and Governor Tarcísio de Freitas announced the Boulevard São João project, aiming to transform a stretch of Avenida São João in the city center into a local 'Times Square' to revitalize the urban area and boost economic and tourist activity.

item.title: Lula fará 2 procedimentos de saúde no Sírio-Libanês, em SP
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will undergo two health procedures at the Sírio-Libanês hospital in São Paulo: a scalp cauterization and an injection for right thumb tendinitis, scheduled for April 24 or 25, 2026. Both procedures are quick and have no post-procedure restrictions. In February, he had previously undergone a cauterization to treat actinic keratosis.

item.title: Zema posta vídeo e mostra que não sabe onde fica o Palácio da Alvorada
item.description: Romeu Zema, a presidential pre-candidate from the NOVO party, posted a video in which he confused the Palácio do Planalto with the Palácio da Alvorada while criticizing Lula’s international travel expenses. He claimed Lula spent R$ 812,000 on luxury hotel accommodation in Germany for two days and called for an end to the 'untouchables’ spending spree,' also supporting ministerial impeachments and criticizing congressional spending.

item.title: STF extrapola ao incluir Zema em inquérito das fake news, diz Caiado
item.description: Former Goiás governor and presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) defended Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) after the STF included Zema in a fake news investigation. Caiado called the measure an overreach by the Supreme Federal Court and emphasized that Zema is a potential rival in the 2026 presidential race.

item.title: Lula viaja para SP para fazer dois procedimentos médicos no Hospital Sírio-Libânes
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will travel to São Paulo on Thursday (23) to undergo two minor medical procedures at the Hospital Sírio-Libanês: a new cranial cauterization to treat actinic keratosis and an injection for tendinitis in his right thumb. The procedures will take place between Friday (24) and Saturday (25), with no impact on future commitments, and Lula will stay at his residence in Alto de Pinheiros. He is expected to return to Brasília on Sunday (26) to attend the closing of the 8th National Congress of the Workers’ Party (PT), with his presence to be confirmed the day before.

item.title: Moro sugere a Gilmar que deixe Fachin “falar pelo STF”
item.description: Senator Sergio Moro (PL), a pré-candidate for governor of Paraná, criticized recent statements by Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes, calling them 'disastrous'. He suggested that Mendes should let Justice Edson Fachin, the president of the STF, speak on behalf of the Court. The remarks followed a series of interviews by Mendes that Moro said damaged the institution's image.

item.title: Elite dirigente quer manter população no escuro, diz Lula
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva denounced that the country's ruling elite seeks to keep the population in the darkness of disinformation and ignorance during the Vivaleitura Prize ceremony in Brasília. He emphasized that the government is expanding the MEC Livros platform from 8,000 to 25,000 titles and signed with the Ministers of Culture and Education the new PNLL 2026-2035, aiming to increase the population's reading habit from 47% to 55% by 2035.

item.title: Lava Jato: A nova decisão de Toffoli que beneficia ex-presidente do Panamá
item.description: Supreme Federal Court Minister Dias Toffoli annulled the use of evidence obtained from Odebrecht's leniency agreement, specifically from the Drousys and My Web Day B systems, in a case against former Panamanian president Ricardo Martinelli Berrocal. The April 17, 2026 order prohibits Brazilian authorities from using such evidence in investigative acts or international cooperation, reinforcing his March 2024 ruling. The directive applies to Brazil's legal order and was forwarded to the Ministry of Justice.

item.title: Lula fará 2 procedimentos médicos no hospital Sírio-Libanês, em SP
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) will be admitted to the Sírio-Libanês Hospital in São Paulo on Thursday, the 23rd, to undergo two simple medical procedures. The Presidency’s Secretariat of Communication confirmed the exams will take place between Friday, the 24th, and Saturday, the 25th. There is no indication of seriousness regarding the procedures.

item.title: Deputado explica por que Flávio Bolsonaro deve ‘surpreender’ nas próximas pesquisas
item.description: Deputy Filipe Barros (PL) states that Flávio Bolsonaro’s strategy of presenting himself as more moderate in the 2026 election is natural and reflects his existing political profile, not an artificial construct. He emphasizes Lula’s growing rejection, the ease of uniting the right and center-right, and the inevitability of a judicial reform debate as key factors that could lead Flávio to 'surprise' in the polls, despite internal divisions within the conservative camp.

item.title: Lula passará por dois procedimentos cirúrgicos nesta sexta
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will undergo two medical procedures this Friday, the 25th, at the Sírio-Libanês Hospital in São Paulo: removal of a scalp keratose and an injection in the right wrist to treat thumb tendinitis. The Presidency's Secretariat of Communication confirmed the schedule, which does not indicate seriousness. The procedures are routine and aimed at health maintenance.

item.title: Lula passa por dois procedimentos médicos no Sírio-Libanês nesta sexta-feira
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will undergo two medical procedures at the Sírio-Libanês Hospital on Friday, May 24: removal of a keratosis on his head and an injection in his right wrist to treat tendinitis. The Presidency stated the interventions are simple, require no rest, and will not result in physical restrictions. Lula is expected to return to Brasília on Sunday to attend a Workers' Party congress.

item.title: ‘Times Square’ de SP: Tarcísio se junta a Nunes para anunciar versão turbinada de projeto que levará painéis de LED ao centro
item.description: Mayor Ricardo Nunes and Governor Tarcísio de Freitas unveiled an enhanced version of the 'Boulevard São João' project, dubbed 'Times Square paulistana', featuring four LED panels, weekend street closures, and cultural and gastronomic programming. The governor boosted the project’s visibility after sharing an AI-generated video, emphasizing state-municipal collaboration in urban renewal, although the initiative is led by the city hall. Despite tensions with the Clean City Law, the project aims for completion by end of September.

item.title: Governo envia ao Congresso plano para baixar gasolina com arrecadação do petróleo
item.description: The Lula government has submitted a bill to Congress allowing tax reductions on fuels such as gasoline and ethanol when there is an extraordinary increase in oil revenue. The measure aims to cushion the domestic impact of rising international oil prices due to the Middle East conflict by converting part of the fiscal gain into direct consumer relief, initially focusing on gasoline, which still carries R$ 0,47 per liter in federal taxes.

item.title: Lula vai a SP para passar por procedimentos na cabeça e no punho
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will undergo medical procedures in São Paulo on Friday to remove a skin growth (keratosis) on his head and receive an injection to treat tendonitis in his right thumb. The government says the procedures are minor and will not require rest, allowing Lula to fulfill official commitments in São Paulo’s interior and attend the PT’s National Congress in Brasília over the weekend.

item.title: PT, PV e PCdoB pedem suspensão de perfil feito por IA com críticas a Lula
item.description: The PT, PV, and PCdoB parties filed a representation with the TSE to suspend the 'Dona Maria' social media profiles, which use an AI-generated character to criticize President Lula. They argue the accounts spread disinformation and misuse AI to damage his image.

item.title: Van Hattem acusa Gilmar de “xenofobia” e “homofobia” contra Zema
item.description: Federal deputy Marcel van Hattem (Novo-RS) accused Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes of xenophobia toward people from Minas Gerais and homophobia toward former Minas governor Romeu Zema (Novo), stating Mendes 'is not well'. The allegations came amid Mendes' public criticisms of politicians from the Novo party.

item.title: Lula faz procedimentos na pele e no punho nesta sexta (24) em São Paulo
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, 80, will undergo two medical procedures this Friday (24) in São Paulo: skin cauterization and a wrist injection to relieve pain in his right thumb. The procedures are routine and aimed at addressing age-related discomfort and repetitive strain.

item.title: Governo negocia solução para dívidas do agro sem pré-sal e com prazo de seis anos
item.description: The Lula government is negotiating a solution for agribusiness debt without using the R$30 billion from the pre-salt Social Fund, as requested by the sector. Finance Minister Dario Durigan proposed an alternative based on securitization with a six-year repayment term. The plan aims to meet agribusiness demands while preserving strategic public resources.

item.title: TSE decide que proibição a voto de presos provisórios não valerá em 2026
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) ruled that new rules restricting the vote of pretrial and temporary detainees will not apply in the 2026 elections. As a result, voter registration and the installation of voting sections in prison units remain valid for this year's election. The decision ensures these individuals can continue to exercise their right to vote.

item.title: Governo Lula propõe usar receita extra com petróleo para cortar impostos sobre combustíveis
item.description: The Lula government proposed to Congress using extraordinary oil revenues to cut taxes on fuels, such as PIS/Cofins and CIDE, to mitigate the impact of the Iran war on domestic prices. Announced by Finance Minister Dario Durigan, the measure involves a cost of R$30.5 billion, but the government claims no fiscal impact due to the use of excess revenues. The bill was filed by the government leader in the Chamber, Deputy Paulo Pimenta (PT-RS).

item.title: Lula vai a São Paulo para fazer cauterização na cabeça e infiltração por causa de tendinite na mão
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva travels to São Paulo for two medical procedures: cauterization to remove a scalp keratosis and an injection in his right wrist to treat thumb tendonitis. Both are scheduled for Friday at the Sírio-Libanês Hospital, with no prior preparation or contraindications. Afterward, he will rest at his Pinheiros residence through Saturday; his attendance at the PT Congress closing in Brasília on Sunday remains unconfirmed, and on Monday he will undertake interior São Paulo engagements, including inaugurations in Presidente Prudente and Andradina.

item.title: PT, PV e PC do B acionam TSE contra o perfil “Dona Maria”
item.description: The PT, PV, and PC do B parties filed a complaint with the TSE seeking the suspension of social media profiles identified as 'Dona Maria', which use AI-generated imagery of an elderly woman to spread political disinformation targeting Lula, the left, and the STF, while promoting Bolsonaro-aligned narratives. They argue the profiles fail to consistently disclose their AI nature, misleading users into believing the character is real, and may be monetized through advertising partnerships, violating electoral laws on anonymous political propaganda.

item.title: Lula fará retirada de acúmulo de pele na cabeça e infiltração no punho para tratar tendinite, diz Planalto
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will undergo medical procedures in São Paulo on Friday (24) to remove a skin accumulation (keratosis) on his head and receive an injection in his right wrist to treat tendinitis. The government states the procedures are simple and require no rest, with his official engagements postponed to Monday (27). Lula is expected to return to Brasília on Sunday (26) to attend a Workers' Party congress.

item.title: Romeu Zema cresce no conflito com Gilmar Mendes e aumenta desgaste do STF
item.description: The conflict between Minister Gilmar Mendes and former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) is increasing wear on the Supreme Court while boosting Zema's political visibility, according to columnist Fernando Schüler, who cites the Barbra Streisand effect. The tension raises concerns about censorship of political humor and satire in Brazil, warning that treating criticism as an attack on the rule of law could lead to an Orwellian regime. Zema is gaining prominence in the 2026 electoral race, with increased engagement and attention due to the judicial dispute.

item.title: Eleitor em Dia: prazo para tirar o título antes do fechamento do cadastro se encerra em 6 de maio
item.description: The deadline to obtain a voter ID, transfer electoral domicile, update registration data, or regularize electoral pendings ends on May 6, 2025. After this date, the electoral registry will be closed for the 2026 Elections. Services are available online via the TSE Portal or in person at electoral offices, with biometric procedures requiring in-person attendance.

item.title: O novo capítulo da troca de farpas entre Gilmar Mendes e Romeu Zema
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes mocked the accent of former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema, likening it to a Timorese dialect in a Record TV interview. Zema responded on social media, accusing Mendes of losing moral clarity and using authoritarianism to suppress criticism. The conflict arose after Mendes requested Zema be investigated in the fake news inquiry over an animation depicting him as corrupt.

item.title: TSE aprova transferência de R$ 13 milhões para Itamaraty organizar eleições no exterior
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) unanimously approved the transfer of R$ 13.2 million to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Itamaraty) to rent properties abroad for the 2026 presidential elections, aiming to accommodate 65 electoral sections in countries where Brazilian embassies or consulates lack capacity. The funding supports voting access for approximately 793,330 Brazilians registered overseas, a figure that has steadily increased since 2010. The TSE must designate the sections by July 6, and Itamaraty must request additional sections by June 22.

item.title: Lideranças femininas acompanham sessão do TSE desta quinta (23)
item.description: Over 70 female leaders attended the TSE session to monitor rulings and advocate for the 30% gender quota in candidacies. They stressed that combating feminicide and domestic violence must be permanent political priorities, not just election-season topics. Stafanie Lucena and Yannahe Marques shared personal testimonies to underscore that women's political participation is vital for repairing social harm and saving lives.

item.title: Projeto aperfeiçoa decisão de investimento na previdência complementar
item.description: PLP 87/2026, proposed by Senator Esperidião Amin (PP-SC), seeks to require an absolute majority in the deliberative council of closed pension entities to approve investments of 5% or more of guarantor resources, banning the chair’s tie-breaking vote. The initiative aims to strengthen governance and mitigate financial risks while preserving the LC 108/2001 framework.

item.title: Governo volta atrás e diz que não vai reduzir imposto da gasolina
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan stated that the Lula government will not announce a reduction in federal taxes on gasoline, despite earlier communications indicating such an announcement was planned to counter international fuel price increases. He clarified that the press conference was intended to discuss a mechanism under consideration in Congress to enable future tax reductions, not to implement an immediate cut, and that no formal announcement had ever been made. Planning Minister Bruno Moretti criticized media coverage for framing the situation as a 'retreat', noting that a complementary bill had been submitted to Congress to establish a neutral fiscal regime for fuel tax reductions.

item.title: “Imagina que comecemos a fazer bonecos do Zema como homossexual”, diz Gilmar
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes criticized satirical cartoons by former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema depicting him and Justice Dias Toffoli, stating that creating similar caricatures of Zema as homosexual would be equally offensive.
